narrative:
The model estimates a 66% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This prediction is driven primarily by three key factors in your profile.

Your relatively short overall work experience of 1-5 years was the strongest factor pulling the prediction toward leaving. Among employees the model expected to stay, only about half had similarly limited experience, while the rest had six or more years. This limited tenure appears to signal higher turnover risk to the model.

The second most influential factor was that you have received other job offers while working here. This strongly pushed the prediction toward leaving, as having external opportunities often indicates that someone is considering or actively exploring moves elsewhere.

Your employment in the “other” sector was the third important driver and also increased the likelihood of leaving. Only 22% of employees predicted to stay work in this broad category, compared with much higher shares in medical or education fields.

Although several positive aspects exist in your profile, such as receiving a bonus, feeling you got deserved promotions, and reporting recognition from superiors, the model weighed your shorter experience, external opportunities, and sector most heavily.

The organization should discuss retention strategies with you, while you may want to reflect on whether your current role still aligns with your longer-term goals. Addressing these specific concerns could change the outlook for future opportunities.
